text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak said that Israeli settlement expansion in Arab occupied lands would further complicate the Middle East problem and torpedo the Palestinian cause.
"There are forces in Sudan, that are trading in terrorism," Mubarak told a meeting of senior military officers.
- The Parliament endorsed an agreement with Pakistan on security cooperation and extradition of criminals.
- 190 million pounds appropriated for work to start in the next 48 hours digging Sheikh Zaid canal in the western desert.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid:Nine million shares in two cement companies will be offered for sale on international stock markets. Shares in 14 firms will be sold off within the coming few days.

- Public Works & Water Resources Minister Abdel Hadi Radi was admitted to hospital after returning from Paris. Egypt Air hospital director, Muhie Hammad, said Radi was suffering from severe anaemia and general debilitation.
- Mubarak told senior military officers:We can not stand still in front of what is exposing the region to destabilisation.
